steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest deadline is six days after Saturday, October 24, 2026, which is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT. Pacific Time (PT) on this date is UTC-7 ( Daylight Saving Time still active until November 1, 2026). Madrid is in UTC+1 (Standard Time, as daylight saving ended on October 25, 2026). The time difference between PT (UTC-7) and Madrid (UTC+1) is 8 hours. Converting 11:59 PM PT to Madrid time: 11:59 PM + 8 hours = 7:59 AM on the next day (Saturday, October 31, 2026).

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest closes on Monday, November 2, 2026, at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time (UTC-8). Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) in early November 2026. The time difference is 9 hours (UTC+1 minus UTC-8 = 9 hours ahead). Converting 10:00 AM PT to Madrid time: 10:00 + 9 = 19:00 (7 PM) on the same day.  
 ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 Madrid time (CEST, UTC+2). Converting this to UTC gives 16:00 UTC. Adding 48 hours results in 16:00 UTC on October 26, 2026. On October 25, 2026, daylight saving time ends in Madrid (last Sunday of October), so the time zone switches to CET (UTC+1) starting October 25. Thus, 16:00 UTC on October 26 converts to 17:00 CET (UTC+1) in Madrid local time.

 ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest starts on October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT (UTC-7). The deadline is 72 hours later, which is October 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT. Madrid is in CET (UTC+1) on this date (Daylight Saving time ended on October 25, 2026). The time difference between PT (UTC-7) and Madrid (UTC+1) is 8 hours. Adding 8 hours to 10:00 AM PT gives 6:00 PM (18:00) in Madrid time.

 ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The submission closes on October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET (UTC-4, as daylight saving time is still in effect in the U.S.). Converting this to UTC gives November 1, 2026, at 03:59 UTC. Adding 36 hours results in November 2, 2026, at 15:59 UTC. Madrid operates on CET (UTC+1) on this date (since daylight saving time ended on October 25, 2026). Thus, 15:59 UTC + 1 hour = 16:59 CET on November 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The Unix timestamp 1791788340 corresponds to UTC time. Converting this to a readable date:  
- 1791788340 seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC equals **2026-10-11 06:59:00 UTC**.  
- Tokyo is UTC+9, so adding 9 hours gives **2026-10-11 15:59 JST**.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-11 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid observes Central European Time ( CET, UTC+1 ) during standard time and Central European Summer Time ( CEST, UTC+2 ) during daylight saving time. The deadline is given as 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z (UTC). Daylight saving time ends in Spain on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), at 3:00 AM CEST (equivalent to 1:00 UTC), when clocks are set back to 2:00 AM CET. Since the UTC deadline (02:30) occurs ** after ** the time change (1:00 UTC), Madrid is in CET (UTC+1) at that moment. Converting 02:30 UTC to CET: 02:30 + 1 hour = 03:30 local time.

 ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is 11:59 PM Pacific Time (UTC-7) on the last Sunday of October 2026. The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25th. Pacific Daylight Time (UTC-7) converts to UTC by adding 7 hours, resulting in 6:59 UTC on October 26th. Spain observes Central European Time (UTC+1) after the daylight saving time switch on October 25th ( which occurs at 3am CEST, turning to 2am CET). Thus, 6:59 UTC on October 26th is 7:59 AM CET in Madrid.  
ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026. In the US, daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday of November. November 1, 2026, is a Sunday (calculated via day-of-week arithmetic), making it the correct date. On this day, at 12:00 noon, the time zone switches to EST (UTC-5) after the 2 AM change. Lima, Peru, operates on UTC- year-round with no daylight saving time. Thus, the local time in Lima matches the Eastern Time (UTC-5) deadline exactly.

 ANSWer: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) corresponds to UTC-12. A deadline of "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" is equivalent to **00:00 UTC on January 1, 2027** (since 24:00 on a given day is midnight of the next day). Converting UTC to Tokyo time (UTC+9):  
00:00 UTC + 9 hours = **09:00 on January 1, 2027**? Wait, no. Wait:  
- AoE time: 24:00 on December 31, 2026 (UTC-12) = 12:00 UTC on January 1, 2027 (because adding 12 hours to UTC-12 time gives UTC time: 24:00 + 12h = 36:00, which is 12:00 next day in UTC).  
- Tokyo is UTC+9, so 12:00 UTC + 9h = **21:00 on January 1, 2027**.  

Correct calculation:  
- AoE (UTC-12) time: 24:00 Dec 31, 2026 = 12:00 UTC Jan 1, 2027.  
- Tokyo time: 12:00 UTC + 9h = 21:00 Jan 1, 2027.  

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney time (AED UTC+11) on October 5, 2026, is 5:00 PM. Madrid time (CEst UTC+2) is 9 hours behind Sydney. Subtracting 9 hours from 5:00 PM Sydney time gives 8:00 AM Madrid time on the same day.  
ANSWER: 2026-10-05 08:00
